Okay, here is the translation as promised:

Preface:

Before you scroll to the statistics, some basic questions need to be answered. This is essential to understand the numbers and to be able to judge them.

  • What kind of statistic is this and what does it say?

A crime suspect quota per nationality of chosen countries of origin and selected crimes, which are relevant for the current migrant discussion. It's a snapshot of the situation in the year 2014 in Germany. This statistic does not provide any explanations or thougts on how and why each country came to it's quota. This statistic only provides bare data, which has been calculated from freely accessible, official statistic material.

  • Which sources have been used for this statistic, and why is it for 2014 and not for 2015?

The BKA annually publishes a police criminal statistic(PKS). Part of which is table 62: "Crimes and nationality of nongerman crime suspects". The population of the 21.12.2014 was used for calculation the crime suspect quota for each nationality. Data for 2015 does not exist yet. As soon as it does, it will be possible to compare it to the data of 2014 in order to see in how far the current migration has influenced the statistic.

  • "Crime suspects"? Does that carry any weight?

Despite the original intention of this expression, the admission of a crimes suspect into the PKS does not work like this: -> kiosk robbery -> "I bet it was these two guys x and y, officer!" -> and bam, you have to crime suspects with a xyz nationality. Admission criteria can be seen on the homepage of the BKA here: Publikationen>Polizeiliche Kriminalstitistik>Allgemeine Hinweise zur PKS

  • Why were specific crimes chosen for this statistic and not all of them?

The focus was on crimes, which are relevant for the current debate. On top of that, there are crimes which are specific for foreign people like violation of residence law, which would distort the statistic of certain countries a lot, but wouldn't really say anything aboit the actual consequences for society. Providing statistic proof, that immigrants from certain countries infringe upon immigration or residence laws more than others, is absurd witch respect to commonly known routes and facts.

  • Why is the calculation made per capita and does not show a total amount?

A quota is less misleading than a total number. 1.5 million citizens from turkey are necessarily going to commit more crimes than 40.000 brazilians. With few crimes with a low number of cases, like with murder and manslaughter, it would lead to relativization. People would think that it "wasn't so bad" or it would be "acceptable". This would happen if nationalities with only a few people living in Germany had numbers of about 20 death related cases or so. (I fucked this passage up pretty badly, can't think of a better translation). The downside of a quota is though, that for when it comes to nationalities with a low number of people living in germany, a few habitual offenders could inflate the statistic.

  • Which countries of origin where chosen and why?

A minimum of 15.000 people per country should be a given. Otherwise a few habitual offenders would suffice to mess up the statistic for this country. Some european, american and east asian countries were used to provide reference values. To be able to judge the numbers, you have to know, that the quotas for nationalities with a lot of people are tendentially lower and therefore the quotas for nationalities with a low number of people in germany are tendentially higher.

  • I want to check more countries for myself

In this case you need the method for calculation. Get the number of crime suspects from table 62 from the BKA. You can find the chosen values in these lines: 5(murder), 10(manslaughter), 14(sexual offenses), 27(child abuse), 60(robbery), 113(body harm), 366(thievery), and 389(fraud). For calculating the quota you also need the respective population number. You can find this on de.statista.com (Branchen>Gesellschaft>Demographie>Anzahl der Ausländer in Deutschland nach Herkunftsland 2014). If for exampple there were 60.000 people from country xyz in Germany and the PKS shows 4570 crimes suspects for a crime, you calculate: 100/60.000*457 = 7.62 which would be the quota for 100 people from xyz. Calculated for 10.000 people from xyz, this would be 762 crime suspects.

  • Is the calculation free of errors and reputable?

This is not an official statistic. Big outliers were recalculated multiple times and checked. Complete absence of errors can not be guaranteed though. All sources and calculation formulas have been written down though. In case you don't trust any of these numbers, it's no problem to verify it yourself.
